frontier_selector.why: The presence of irregular red lacunae with irregular vessels and absence of septa, along with the histopathological findings of well-circumscribed dermal vascular tumor with ectatic thin-walled vessels and intracytoplasmic eosinophilic hyaline globules, specifically supports Papillary Intralymphatic Angioendothelioma (PILA).

support_spans: irregular red lacunae with irregular vessels and absence of septa
Well-circumscribed dermal vascular tumor extending to the superficial subcutaneous tissue
composed of ectatic thin-walled vessels with multiple intravascular branching papillary structures
Structures covered by swollen endothelial cells with numerous intracytoplasmic eosinophilic hyaline globules
Periodic acid−Schiff (PAS) staining showed positive hyaline globules in the cytoplasm of endothelial cells
contradict_spans: Tumor vessels were positive for CD-31, negative for D2-40 (podoplanin) and HHV-8
